Marissa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple clarifying items from our side:

- Goal: replace our current FAQ-search with a RAG-backed assistant across product docs + contracts. Must minimize hallucinations for legal clauses.
- Latency SLO: ~<500ms median for 98th percentile where possible.
- Scale: ~200k queries/month initially; dataset is ~120k docs (mix of PDFs, HTML, internal notes).
- Security: data never leaves our VPC in production (we'll discuss Private deployment).

I'm attaching a short data profile that Priya put together so you can see doc types and sizes. Please send recommended models, retrieval stack, and an evaluation plan (metrics + sample prompts).

Next steps from us: share prompt examples and a list of high-risk queries (legal/product).



— Alex
VP of Product, ACME Corp

Attachment: ACME-internal-data-profile.pdf (summary, doc counts, types)

> - Goal: replace our current FAQ-search with a RAG-backed assistant across product docs + contracts. Must minimize hallucinations for legal clauses.
> - Latency SLO: ~<500ms median for 98th percentile where possible.
> - Scale: ~200k queries/month initially; dataset is ~120k docs (mix of PDFs, HTML, internal notes).

Thanks Alex — this is super helpful. Quick recap from our side + proposed evaluation plan: 

Recap / constraints
- Grounding is the primary success criteria (precision@k for grounding, hallucination rate).
- We should run tests for both throughput and 95/98p latency against the production-ish dataset you sent.

Recommended starter models (to iterate quickly):
- rw-13b-fp16 (good accuracy; use fp16 on Dedicated/Private)
- rw-7b-quant (lower cost; useful as a fallback for budget-bound queries)
- tiny-cross-encoder (reranker candidate for high-precision tasks)

Retrieval stack suggestions\- Retriever: dense embeddings + FAISS index (HNSW for recall), shard by doc type for speed.
- Embeddings: rw-embed-large or rw-embed-384 for higher precision on legal text.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for legal/contract questions (higher latency but improves grounding).

Evaluation plan (what we'll run together)
1) Create a prompt set of ~150 queries across categories (legal clauses, product, troubleshooting). We'll split into calibration (50) + eval (100).
2) Baselines: top-k retriever + no-rerank; retriever + lightweight bi-encoder rerank; retriever + cross-encoder rerank.
3) Metrics: grounding_precision@1, grounding_precision@3, exact-match for clause extraction, hallucination_rate, token cost, 95/98p latency.
4) Produce a short dashboard and recommended config per workload.

Attachments: I attached a sample prompt set (v1) and a small eval metadata template we'll use for runs. Can you confirm the list of high-risk queries and whether you want us to run these in your VPC or in a dedicated Redwood Private trial?

Proposed next step: 30 min sync next Wed (Jun 23) to align on prompt set and run schedule.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_rag_prompt_set_v1.csv, acme_rag_eval_results_metadata.json

From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: ACME - RAG eval: retriever & reranker next steps

Marissa / Alex —

Adding a few technical notes that we'll need to decide before the eval run:

1) Indexing & retrieval tuning\- Chunking: 750-1500 token chunks for contracts (preserve clause boundaries); use sliding window for long HTML pages.
- Embedding dim: rw-embed-large (1024) for legal precision — tradeoff is index size.
- Index: FAISS HNSW with IVF sharding by doc source (contracts vs product docs).

2) Reranker choices\- Bi-encoder reranker (fast) — good for throughput; will improve recall ordering but limited precision for subtle legal nuance.
- Cross-encoder reranker (slower) — recommended for high-risk legal queries; we can configure to run only for queries flagged as high-risk to control cost/latency.

3) Grounding metrics / thresholding\- We'll compute grounding_precision@1 and apply a confidence threshold. If confidence below threshold, escalate to a fallback path (show "source list" + link rather than a single generated answer).

4) Benchmarks we should produce during the eval\- End-to-end P95 latency (retrieve + rerank + generation), cost-per-query estimate, grounding precision, and a small set of failure cases with trace logs.

I'll prepare a sample Jupyter notebook that runs the pipelines against a subset of ACME docs and share the baseline numbers ahead of the Wed sync.


— Ethan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
